title: Handle ZIP failures during asynchronous initialization
goal: Handle malformed ZIP directories around both the awaited factory and entry traversal; distinguish directory discovery from complete payload validation.

selectionNotes: Handle malformed ZIP directories around both the awaited factory and entry traversal; distinguish directory discovery from complete payload validation.
Older examples are comparisons, not additional catalogue targets.

runtime.name: .NET
runtime.reason: The primary route uses the net11.0 framework/package asset and .NET 11 behavior.

sdk.name: .NET SDK
sdk.reason: Build the declared net11.0 consumer with a matching SDK.

language.name: C#
language.reason: The canonical .NET 11 project selects C# 15; the comparison project selects C# 14.

packageAssets: Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref ref/net11.0 and Microsoft.NETCore.App runtime; framework-supplied APIs, no added NuGet package
platforms: Desktop/server .NET process and stream access. Measured Windows 11 x64; browser/WASI excluded.
prerequisites: Console project with implicit usings and System.IO.Compression; caller-owned readable source stream and a cleanup scope established before the factory await.
constraints: Read-mode directory discovery is separate from complete payload CRC validation and sender authentication. Non-seekable inputs may be buffered.
The caller owns the stream on factory failure/cancellation; this example uses leaveOpen=true and requires caller disposal.
Async-only proof uses a readable seekable stream; .NET 10 Entries can attempt synchronous reads.
stabilityLimitations: Exact RC2 artifacts executed; no GA verification. No experimental annotation or opt-in on the used APIs.

evidence.scope: Real ZIP directory failure timing, async-only read tracking, pre-cancellation, leaveOpen/disposal and damaged Stored-payload EOF behavior.
